Abstract:

Breast cancer is a major health issue, wherein correct delineation of lesions, reliable classification, and integration of heterogeneous clinical information, are important for successful diagnosis and clinical management. However, breast cancer analysis is challenging, due to the heterogeneity in lesion morphology, tissue specific properties, imaging conditions, pathological appearance, and various patient-specific clinical information. Manual interpretation of breast images or pathological information is time consuming, requires intensive expertise to analyze, and introduces inter-observer variability in the process. Computer-assisted analysis can provide quantitative and reliable information however, lesion delineation, benignmalignant discrimination, and utilization of complimentary information from different sources, remains challenging. The proposed research explores the use of machine learning and deep learning based methods for breast cancer analysis. In particular, this research focuses on structure-aware segmentation of breast cancer ultrasound lesions, where the joint learning of semantic, structural, boundary, and geometric information is explored to achieve accurate lesion delineation. Based on this approach, a framework is proposed that achieves a Dice of 0.8882, IoU of&nbsp 0.7965, HD95 of 6.05 pixel, and ASSD of&nbsp 5.27 pixel on the BUSI dataset. Building upon accurate lesion characterization, learning based techniques will be explored to distinguish between benign and malignant breast tumors using discriminative morphological, structural and appearance features. Further, a multimodal learning framework will be proposed to utilize complimentary information from radiological, pathological, and clinical data for comprehensive breast cancer classification. The expected outcome from the proposed research is an integrated framework for AI assisted breast cancer analysis, that can provide accurate lesion delineation, reliable benignmalignant classification and comprehensive multimodal analysis of breast tumors.
